source_text.body:
Monitor feeds for story angles and draft content
A commenter's OpenClaw watches Reddit and news for story angles, drafts content, logs to memory, and pings Telegram, cutting 2-3 hours of work to about 20 minutes of review.
·
Mar 1, 2026
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
In a Reddit comment, the user said they run OpenClaw as a “full business operator” that watches Reddit and news feeds for story angles, drafts content, saves everything into memory files so it can resume across sessions, and sends Telegram alerts when it needs attention. The only human step they described was reviewing the output and deciding whether to ship it.
How it went
They said the payoff was time: work that used to take 2–3 hours of research and writing now takes about 20 minutes of review. They did not give output volume, revenue, or quality metrics beyond that.
Worth knowing
The clearest catch is that the source gives almost no build detail, only the claimed workflow and time savings.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
Every [morning/hour] check [subreddits and news sites] for new stories related to [my topic or beat] and pick the [3-5] with the strongest angles for my audience of [audience]. For each one, write a short draft in my voice ([tone description]) and save it to your memory log so you don't repeat topics. Then send me a summary of the picks on [Telegram/other chat app]. Never publish or post anything; drafts only, for me to review.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/openclaw/comments/1s0y56h/has_anyone_actually_built_anything_useful
